[[File:Inverted snub dodecadodecahedron.stl|thumb|3D model of an inverted snub dodecadodecahedron]]
In [[geometry]], the '''inverted snub dodecadodecahedron''' (or '''vertisnub dodecadodecahedron''') is a [[nonconvex uniform polyhedron]], indexed as U<sub>60</sub>.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mathconsult.ch/static/unipoly/60.html|title=60: inverted snub dodecadodecahedron|last=Roman|first=Maeder|date=|website=MathConsult|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> It is given a [[Schläfli symbol]] {{math|sr{5/3,5}.}} 

==Cartesian coordinates==

Let <math>\xi\approx 2.109759446579943</math> be the largest real zero of the polynomial <math>P=2x^4-5x^3+3x+1</math>. Denote by <math>\phi</math> the [[golden ratio]]. Let the point <math>p</math> be given by
:<math>p=
\begin{pmatrix}
        \phi^{-2}\xi^2-\phi^{-2}\xi+\phi^{-1}\\
        -\phi^{2}\xi^2+\phi^{2}\xi+\phi\\
        \xi^2+\xi
\end{pmatrix}
</math>.
Let the matrix <math>M</math> be given by
:<math>M=
\begin{pmatrix}
         1/2  & -\phi/2 & 1/(2\phi) \\
         \phi/2   & 1/(2\phi)     & -1/2 \\
         1/(2\phi)     & 1/2  & \phi/2
\end{pmatrix}
</math>.
<math>M</math> is the rotation around the axis <math>(1, 0, \phi)</math>  by an angle of <math>2\pi/5</math>, counterclockwise. Let the linear transformations <math>T_0, \ldots, T_{11}</math> 
be the transformations which send a point <math>(x, y, z)</math> to the [[parity of a permutation|even permutations]] of <math>(\pm x, \pm y, \pm z)</math>  with an even number of minus signs. 
The transformations <math>T_i</math> constitute the group of rotational symmetries of a [[regular tetrahedron]].
The transformations <math>T_i M^j</math> <math>(i = 0,\ldots, 11</math>, <math>j = 0,\ldots, 4)</math> constitute the group of rotational symmetries of a [[regular icosahedron]].
Then the 60 points <math>T_i M^j p</math>  are the vertices of a snub dodecadodecahedron. The edge length equals <math>2(\xi+1)\sqrt{\xi^2-\xi}</math>, the circumradius equals <math>(\xi+1)\sqrt{2\xi^2-\xi}</math>, and the midradius equals <math>\xi^2+\xi</math>.

For a great snub icosidodecahedron whose edge length is 1,
the circumradius is
:<math>R = \frac12\sqrt{\frac{2\xi-1}{\xi-1}} \approx 0.8516302281174128</math> 
Its midradius is
:<math>r=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{\xi}{\xi-1}} \approx 0.6894012223976083</math>

The other real root of P plays a similar role in the description of the [[snub dodecadodecahedron]].

== Related polyhedra==

=== Medial inverted pentagonal hexecontahedron===
{{Uniform polyhedra db|Uniform dual polyhedron stat table|Isdid}}
[[File:Medial inverted pentagonal hexecontahedron.stl|thumb|3D model of a medial inverted pentagonal hexecontahedron]]
The '''medial inverted pentagonal hexecontahedron''' (or '''midly petaloid ditriacontahedron''') is a nonconvex [[Isohedral figure|isohedral]] [[polyhedron]]. It is the [[Dual polyhedron|dual]] of the [[uniform star polyhedron|uniform]] inverted snub dodecadodecahedron. Its faces are irregular nonconvex pentagons, with one very acute angle.

==Proportions==

Denote the [[golden ratio]] by <math>\phi</math>, and let <math>\xi\approx -0.236\,993\,843\,45</math> be the largest (least negative) real zero of the polynomial <math>P=8x^4-12x^3+5x+1</math>. Then each face has three equal angles of <math>\arccos(\xi)\approx 103.709\,182\,219\,53^{\circ}</math>, one of <math>\arccos(\phi^2\xi+\phi)\approx 3.990\,130\,423\,41^{\circ}</math> and one of <math>360^{\circ}-\arccos(\phi^{-2}\xi-\phi^{-1})\approx 224.882\,322\,917\,99^{\circ}</math>. Each face has one medium length edge, two short and two long ones. If the medium length is <math>2</math>, then the short edges have length 
<math display=block>1-\sqrt{\frac{1-\xi}{\phi^3-\xi}}\approx 0.474\,126\,460\,54,</math>
and the long edges have length
<math display=block>1+\sqrt{\frac{1-\xi}{\phi^{-3}-\xi}} \approx  37.551\,879\,448\,54.</math>
The [[dihedral angle]] equals <math>\arccos(\xi/(\xi+1))\approx 108.095\,719\,352\,34^{\circ}</math>. The other real zero of the polynomial <math>P</math> plays a similar role for the [[medial pentagonal hexecontahedron]].
